working_title: Breeding-space contraction recurs across declining Adelie and chinstrap penguins
core_claim: Declining breeding populations in two Pygoscelis species and two Antarctic monitoring systems lose effective breeding-component number faster than expected under proportional thinning plus frozen count-error models.
primary_evidence_order: Palmer Adelie discovery: COR, HUM, LIT
prospectively frozen Signy Adelie 22-season independent-system replication
prospectively frozen Signy chinstrap 22-season cross-species replication
secondary_robustness: later frozen Signy Adelie 1998-2009 eight-literal-unit concentration analysis

posthoc_descriptive_only.allowed_interpretation: Palmer concentration involved dominant-unit turnover whereas both Signy species retained and strengthened the initially dominant unit.
posthoc_descriptive_only.prohibited_interpretation: No p-value, causal size effect, or universal large-colony refuge law may be inferred from the descriptive decomposition.

mechanism_boundary: A separate performance-linked redistribution hypothesis is not used to explain the replicated concentration result because its frozen Signy lag-2 replication was unsupported.
No individual movement, public information, prospecting, win-stay/lose-switch, Allee mechanism, predation mechanism, or unique habitat cause is identified.
manuscript_exclusions: Antarctic-wide area x habitat-complex interaction as a main result
beta hierarchy as a headline result
new concentration metrics, thresholds, tuned windows or rescue analyses
stop_rule: No new ecological endpoint may be added to this manuscript. Remaining work is figure construction, source/provenance audits, literature positioning, prose compression and journal formatting.
